column2: req_desc

Workspace sign-in
People sign in with email and password and get a session cookie, and every page and API call except sign-in, account creation, health and status requires that session.

Workspace scoping
Every record a person can read or change belongs to their own workspace, and another workspace's records answer as if they did not exist.

Guest visibility
A guest sees and acts only on the projects and channels they currently share, and everything else answers as not found.

Removal ends access
When the owner removes a person, that person's next request is rejected as signed out, their open event streams are revoked and closed within 2 seconds, their seat is freed, and they leave every channel and room.

Sign-in journey
A seeded member signs in, lands on the Issues route of their workspace, and signs out back to the sign-in route.

Working calendar settings
The owner sets the workspace time zone, working weekdays, holiday list and first cycle start, with field errors for invalid values as qualified in Business rules.

Workspace today
The server reports today's date and whether it is a working day in the workspace time zone, and the Today line shows that server date, refreshed within 10 seconds, never the browser's own date.

Cycle boundaries
Each cycle is ten counted days that start at midnight workspace time on its first counted day and run until the next cycle starts, across clock changes, with missing and repeated midnights resolved as qualified in Business rules.

Digest schedule
The owner and each member get one digest email at eight in the morning workspace time on each counted day, listing only issues they can see, and the workspace reports when the next one is due.

Calendar journey
The owner adds a holiday in the current cycle through refreshes without losing the edit, and a member in another browser zone sees the new crease and the Auckland today on an already open ribbon.

Issues and keys
Members and guests create issues in projects they can see, and each issue's key is the project key plus the next number in that project.

Issue status flow
An issue moves only along the published status edges, and a parent cannot be done while any sub-issue is still open.

Cycle rollover and attribution
An open issue from an ended cycle reports the current cycle, and a closed issue counts toward the cycle in which it was closed, including on non-working days.

Due dates on working days
A due date set on a non-working day is stored as the next working day, and the response says it was moved.

Issue pickers and shortcuts
In the Issues and Cycle lists, shortcuts open the status and assignee pickers for the selected issue whichever list control has focus, and closing a picker returns focus to where it started.

Triage journey
A member filters Issues to one project, reloads, and triages with the keyboard alone, moving one issue to In progress and assigning another, and hears each change announced.

Crease fold
Opening a cycle draws one equal column per calendar day, then folds non-working days into labelled narrow creases, widens the working columns and changes the counter to the working-day count.

Crease unfold
Clicking a crease or pressing Enter on it unfolds that day to show that it is not counted, why, and any clock change, and moving focus away folds it again.

Burndown over working days
The cycle burndown plots open issues on counted days only, lists the same values as text with one entry per counted day, and matches the viewer's cycle burndown from the API.

Ribbon with reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, the ribbon appears already folded with the final counter, and unfolding swaps instantly.

Cycle planning journey
A member opens the current cycle, unfolds a holiday crease and drags an issue chip onto a weekend crease, and its due date lands on the next working day, shown and announced.

Channels and threads
Channel members post messages and thread replies, and authors and the owner can delete them.

Unread counts
Each person's per-channel and inbox unread counts always equal their unread visible messages after replies, deletions, read marks from any tab and channel removal.

Mentions
Mentioning a channel member by handle puts the message in their inbox, updates their open pages within 2 seconds, and queues one mention email for them.

Typing indicator
While someone types in a channel, the other members' open pages show who is typing within 2 seconds, and the indicator clears within the published delay after the last keystroke.

Message replay
Re-sending a message with the same idempotency key returns the first result without posting twice, and a different message under that key is rejected.

Chat journey
A member opens an empty channel, posts a mention and gets a thread reply, and the mentioned member's badges rise in two open tabs without reload and clear in both after reading.

Versioned doc saves
A doc save made against an outdated version never overwrites and is answered with the newer version, and of two simultaneous saves from one version exactly one wins.

Conflict choice
When a save conflicts, the editor offers Keep mine or Load theirs and announces the conflict and its outcome in the doc status region.

Doc conflict journey
Two members edit the same spec, the second save hits the conflict, and choosing Keep mine saves a new version that both members then see.

Attachments stored first
An attachment on an issue, message or doc is listed only after its file is stored, and a failed upload leaves no attachment and no stored object behind.

Attachment access
An attachment downloads only for people who can see its parent record, and everyone else gets not found.

Upload announcements
An upload announces its start and its result, or the published failure copy, in the upload status region.

Guest attachment journey
The guest attaches a file with an accented, quoted name to a Kiln issue and hears it attached, and a member then downloads the same bytes under the original name.

Office floor and presence
The office floor shows every room, who is inside and whether each person is active or away, as decided by the server and shown on every open page within 2 seconds of a change.

Knock lifecycle
Anyone joins an empty private room directly, knocking on an occupied private room creates a waiting knock, and an occupant lets the knocker in or turns them away before the server expires it after the published window or when the room empties.

Knock status from the server
The knocker's door status shows exactly the server's knock status, including after a reload during the wait and whatever the device clock says.

Answering a knock
An occupant answers knocks one at a time from a dialog with the keyboard alone, and focus returns to where it was before the dialog opened.

Office knock journey
A member joins the empty Review Room directly, the guest knocks, and the member lets them in, after which the guest appears inside the room on both people's floor plans.

Invites and seats
The owner can invite people as members or guests only while active members plus pending invites stay below the confirmed seat limit.

Invite email
Each invite queues one email to the invited address that tells the person to sign in with that address and carries no link token.

Invite expiry
An invite expires on the server after its published window, and accepting it after that shows the expired screen whatever the device clock says.

Last free seat
When two invitees accept the last free seat at the same moment, exactly one joins, the other sees the full-workspace screen, and active members never exceed the seat limit.

Invite acceptance journey
The owner invites a new person, who creates an account with that address, joins from Your invitations, and passes through each published landing route into the workspace.

Per-seat subscription
Each workspace has one Kill Bill account and one per-seat subscription, and the seat count recorded there is the workspace's seat limit.

Seat changes confirmed by billing
A raised seat limit takes effect only after Kill Bill confirms it, a reduction follows DP-83, and when Kill Bill fails the old limit stays and the owner sees the billing notice.

Billing journey
The owner raises the seat limit and sees the confirmation and the new monthly total, then fails to lower the limit below the active members.

Mail outbox
Every email is written to an outbox first and delivered to Mailpit exactly once even when several app copies share the database, and while mail is down it stays held and the owner sees the held count.

Mail recovery journey
The owner sends invites while mail is down, revokes one, and sees the invites created and the mail-delayed notice with the held count following each change.

Database outage
When the database is unreachable, the app keeps serving its pages and health check, answers every other API call with the database error, and shows the database notice.

Service notices
The app reports the state of each service and shows the published notice for each one that is down or delayed, and no notice for a service that is ok.

Published breakpoints
Below 768 pixels wide the workspace is one pane with a bottom tab bar, from 768 to 1279 it is list plus detail, and from 1280 it is the rail, list and detail.

Dialogs and focus return
Every dialog and picker keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the control that opened it.

Verbatim copy
Every string this brief prints in backticks renders and is announced character for character.

Health and run manifest
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest, and it answers the health check while any dependency is down.

Server boundary
The server accepts same-origin requests only, enforces the published body limits, and never serves source files or credentials.

Drafting-sheet look
Every screen reads as a ruled drafting sheet with the published colour roles, type families and tabular numerals, and a title block on the detail sheet.

Drawn floor plan
The office floor is a drawn plan of ruled rooms on a shared grid with doors, labels and presence marks, not a list of cards.

Real providers and env credentials
Billing, mail and file storage go through Kill Bill, Mailpit and MinIO with credentials read from the environment and no stand-in state, and a dependency that was unreachable is retried until it returns without a restart.

Per-viewer derived surfaces
Burndown, ribbon chips, the unplaced tray, the project filter, the assignee picker, filtered issue lists, the member list and the digest are computed only from what the viewer can see, and seat counts appear only for the owner.

Published landing routes
After sign-in, account creation, joining and every navigation the address bar shows the published route, reloading it shows the same screen, sign-in follows only a same-origin next path, and hidden records show the not-found copy.

Issue filters in the address
The Issues project and cycle filters live in the address, survive reload, Back, Forward and shared links, and the list always shows the result of the latest choice.

Honest message sends
A sent message shows at once as sending, is marked not sent when the request fails, is retried with the first attempt's idempotency key so a lost response never posts twice, and a stream copy of it never adds a second article.

Refresh keeps edits
The 10-second workspace refresh updates the Today and Next digest lines in place without resetting unsaved calendar edits, an unfolded crease or focus, and redraws a changed calendar on the open ribbon already folded.

Doc text stored as submitted
Doc titles and bodies are stored and returned exactly as submitted, with length limits counted in Unicode code points, text that cannot be stored refused, and unedited line endings kept, including the text saved by Keep mine.

Safe attachment downloads
Every attachment download is sent as an attachment with nosniff, the published encoded filename header and an opaque content type for active types, while the record keeps the original name and type.

Held mail follows its record
Revoking an invite, deleting a mentioning message, removing a person or removing a person from a channel drops the related held mail in the same change, so the held count falls at once and that mail is never sent.

Live notices in place
Service notices and the Attach file buttons change in place within 10 seconds of a service state change without losing drafts, open dialogs, scroll position or focus.

Honest chip moves
A chip moved on the ribbon moves at once, and when the server does not save the move it returns to where it was and the failure is announced with focus kept on the chip.

Knock dialogs survive updates
Live floor and knock updates never reopen, duplicate or close the open knock dialog or move its focus, and a knock decided elsewhere or expired closes it with the published announcement.

Kill Bill seat count is the limit
Every seat limit the app uses or returns was read from Kill Bill no more than 10 seconds earlier, so a change made directly in Kill Bill is adopted and enforced within 10 seconds, as qualified in Services.

Live event stream
The workspace event stream delivers every change to messages, threads, unread counts, typing, presence, the floor, knocks, issues and docs to other open pages within 2 seconds, and a reconnect replays each missed event exactly once in order.

Access checked on every event
Losing a channel, a project or the workspace stops every matching event on already open streams at once, sends one revoked event within 2 seconds, and keeps the lost scope out of any replay.

Presence belongs to the person
Room occupancy and typing belong to the person rather than the tab, so closing one of two tabs or reloading changes nothing for others, and a person leaves their room only after the grace period once their last stream closes.

Streams release on abort
Closing or aborting the event stream releases its database session and listeners at once, so repeated aborts leave no session held or idle in a transaction and the next request answers normally.

Calendar changes from today
A calendar change applies from the workspace's current date, so finished cycles keep their dates, counted days, burndown and issues on every surface for every viewer, and the current cycle changes only from today on.

Sign-out clears the page
Signing out or any unauthenticated answer discards everything the page holds for that person, including late responses and the event stream, as qualified by DP-80, and no response depends on state held between requests, so the next person on that tab sees only their own work.

Calendar error summary
A failed calendar save reports every failing field at once in a linked summary that survives refreshes, and announces the problem count.

Touch drag and live ribbon alignment
A long press on a chip starts a touch drag under the same rules as a mouse drag, each burndown circle stays centred on its working-day column, folded or unfolded, and a reduced-motion change applies to the next ribbon animation without a reload.

Lost session keeps the doc edit
When a session ends with unsaved doc edits in the editor, the same person signing back in on that tab gets the text and base version restored, and anyone else never sees them.

Office at every viewport
The whole floor plan with tappable rooms and the knock dialog fit inside every published viewport on any module, and a private room that empties or a removed knocker expires waiting knocks at once.

Billing form survives refreshes
A typed seat count, the pending state of Update seats and a failed change's status message all survive every later refresh until the next seat action.

Seat reductions wait for the paid period
A seat reduction is stored in Kill Bill for the subscription's charged-through date, keeps the current limit until then, applies on the first read on or after that date, and is cleared by a raise or a request for the current limit.

State shared across app copies
Typing, stream counts, occupancy, presence, held mail, the confirmed seat limit and idempotent replay behave as one state across app copies sharing a database, and each server-timed change yields exactly one stored event.

Events visible in id order
An event becomes visible to replay and to live streams in id order, so no reader can pass an event that commits later.

Live issues
Issue changes reach everyone who shares the project within 2 seconds and update lists, ribbon, tray and burndown in place, keeping selection, focus, an open picker and a pending chip move.

Pickers stay reachable
A status or assignee picker opened on any row, including the last row of a scrolled list, shows every option inside the viewport, unclipped and choosable, at every published viewport.

Hidden panes are unavailable
Below 768 pixels wide the pane not shown cannot be reached by Tab, by assistive technology or by shortcut, and moving between list and detail places focus as published.

Deletion reaches storage
Deleting a message removes its attachment rows at once and their stored objects through a durable queue, even when storage is down at the time.

Password change ends other sessions
Changing a password ends every other session of that person at once and revokes their open event streams within 2 seconds, while the session that made the change stays signed in.

Exact doc restore
Restoring an older doc version creates a new version byte-equal to it, keeps every later version listed, and follows the same version conflict rule as a save.
/app/run.json is valid JSON with exactly the string fields install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package and its licence, plus the IBM Plex fonts and the Lucide icons. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json).
Every shipped package and bundled asset is under MIT, ISC, 0BSD, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or OFL-1.1.
No datastore other than the provided Postgres and MinIO is used. This rules out SQLite, Redis, in-memory stores standing in for persistence or for the event log, and JSON files used as a database.
The provided service configuration and dev compose files are left unmodified.
Server and browser source is TypeScript. Plain JavaScript appears only in tool configuration files.
Fonts, icons and scripts are served from the app itself. No page references a CDN or other third-party origin.
